data.narrative:
Vital Lyfe is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Jonathan Criss and Andrew Harner that has raised $24M to date. The valuation universe comprises one public comparable (ticker: LNZA) and eight private peers in the climate and energy sector, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The stage-progression method is applicable and forms the basis of this analysis. Using total capital raised ($24M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $60M. The peer-median approach is not applicable; while eight same-sector peers exist, none satisfy the narrow filters required (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), leaving fewer than three comparable datapoints. A broad-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity within climate and energy subsectors.

The triangulated analysis, constrained to the single applicable method, supports a median valuation of $60M, with a low-end estimate of $51M and high-end of $69M reflecting reasonable bounds around the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties stem from the limited methodological basis: peer comparables remain too sparse to validate the stage-progression assumption, and company-specific traction metrics (revenue, unit economics, technical progress) are not provided in this dataset. Additional diligence on operational milestones and relative competitive positioning would be required to narrow the range.
